doc.title: Nancy Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Greatest performance and defining success
summary: Opening night at the Coconut Grove was her greatest performance; success is contentment.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: You had a song called The Greatest Performance. Looking back over your career, is there a greatest performance of your life?
Opening night at the Coconut Grove.

Oh yeah, but you asked me to be specific. I’m telling you – because that was what did everything, that changed it. I had played Las Vegas before I played the Coconut Grove. I’d broken the show in before that. But that night – if that night was successful, then I would be where I am today at 70-whatever. It gave me the longevity that you would want in this career.
What is your definition of success?

Oh dear. A good night’s sleep? I don’t really know. It’s personal. It is not about the business. My definition of success is if I’m content and can sleep at night, and I’m there for my grandchildren. That’s what it’s about.
